def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    import numpy as np
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    N = 60
    dt = duration_s/(N-1)
    points = np.empty((n_runs, N, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    # Initialize all runs at start location, zero time
    points[:, 0, 0] = start[0]
    points[:, 0, 1] = start[1]
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0

    # Constants
    m_lat = terrain.m_lat
    m_lon = terrain.m_lon

    # We will store current pos in lat, lon for each run
    lat = np.full(n_runs, start[0], dtype=np.float64)
    lon = np.full(n_runs, start[1], dtype=np.float64)
    t = np.zeros(n_runs, dtype=np.float64)

    # We simulate over N-1 time steps
    for i in range(1, N):
        elev = terrain.elev(lat, lon)
        slope = terrain.slope_deg(lat, lon)
        # Calculate elevation slightly behind (previous step) to determine movement direction
        if i == 1:
            # At first step, no past movement: approximate gradient direction by finite difference slightly forward
            # We offset a bit downhill direction:
            # We use a small step in lat and lon to estimate gradient vector (steepest descent)
            dlat = 0.00001  # ~1m in lat
            dlon = 0.00001  # ~1m in lon
            elev_north = terrain.elev(lat + dlat, lon)
            elev_south = terrain.elev(lat - dlat, lon)
            elev_east = terrain.elev(lat, lon + dlon)
            elev_west = terrain.elev(lat, lon - dlon)
            # gradients in metres per degree approx
            grad_lat = (elev_north - elev_south) / (2*dlat)
            grad_lon = (elev_east - elev_west) / (2*dlon)
            # convert gradients in metres per degree to slope vector in metres per metre
            grad_lat_m = grad_lat / m_lat
            grad_lon_m = grad_lon / m_lon
            # slope vector points downhill, gradient points uphill, so downhill bearing vector (x,y) in metres:
            # This vector is gradient projected on map meters north/east
            slope_v = np.stack((grad_lat_m, grad_lon_m), axis=-1)
            # downhill bearing vector = -slope_v normalized
            norms = np.linalg.norm(slope_v, axis=-1)
            zero_mask = (norms == 0)
            slope_dir = np.zeros_like(slope_v)
            slope_dir[~zero_mask] = -slope_v[~zero_mask]/norms[~zero_mask,None]
            # Bearings radians: arctan2(east,north)
            # north component = slope_dir[:,0], east component = slope_dir[:,1]
            bearing = np.arctan2(slope_dir[:,1], slope_dir[:,0]) # radians
        else:
            # Movement direction vector from previous step
            dlat_move = lat - points[:,i-1,0]
            dlon_move = lon - points[:,i-1,1]
            # bearing of movement = arctan2(dlon*meters per degree east, dlat*meters per degree north)
            d_east = dlon_move * m_lon
            d_north = dlat_move * m_lat
            norms = np.hypot(d_north, d_east)
            zero_mask = (norms == 0)
            bearing = np.zeros(n_runs, dtype=np.float64)
            bearing[~zero_mask] = np.arctan2(d_east[~zero_mask], d_north[~zero_mask])

        # Backtracking hypothesis: detecting steep slope ahead, revert bearing 180 deg
        # Check slope at current location; if slope >= 30° backtrack (reverse dir)
        backtrack_mask = (slope >= 30)
        bearing = np.where(backtrack_mask, (bearing + np.pi) % (2*np.pi), bearing)

        # Movement speed depends on slope (tobler speed)
        # We approximate d_elev and d_horiz corresponding to moving dt along bearing with 1 m step:
        # We take elevation difference over step size to get gradient approx
        # Use elevation uphill derivative by offsetting forward by 1m along bearing
        lat_fwd, lon_fwd = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing, 1.0)
        elev_fwd = terrain.elev(lat_fwd, lon_fwd)
        d_elev = elev_fwd - elev
        d_horiz = 1.0
        speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev, d_horiz)  # m/s

        # Distance moved this timestep
        dist = speed * dt  # m
        # Limit max step to 30 (one cell) for stability in case of extreme speeds
        dist = np.minimum(dist, 30.0)

        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing, dist)

        # Clamp to terrain box
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.clamp(lat_new, lon_new)

        lat = lat_new
        lon = lon_new
        t += dt

        points[:, i, 0] = lat
        points[:, i, 1] = lon
        points[:, i, 2] = t

    ok = terrain.inside(points[:, -1, 0], points[:, -1, 1])
    return points, ok
